incident: Quantum ransomware (IcedID ISO to domain-wide Quantum in 3h44m)

sources.title: Quantum Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2022-04-25)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (IcedID ISO/LNK docs_invoice_173.iso -> rundll32), hops (WMI cred test to a server, RDP to that server + other servers, PsExec/WMI from DC pivot to all hosts), cred access (LSASS via Task Manager + CS beacon), impact (Quantum ttsel.exe copied to C$ and run via PsExec/WMI), TTR 3h44m

narrative_before: In one of the fastest cases the DFIR Report observed, a 2022 intrusion went from initial access to domain-wide ransomware in 3 hours 44 minutes. Initial access was an IcedID payload in an ISO (docs_invoice_173.iso) delivered by email: the user mounted it and ran document.lnk, executing dar.dll (IcedID) via rundll32. IcedID ran discovery and created a scheduled task; ~2h later Cobalt Strike was injected via process hollowing (into cmd.exe and winlogon.exe), AdFind (adfind.bat) and ns.bat (nslookup per host) ran, and LSASS was accessed (Task Manager and a CS temporary beacon) to steal administrator credentials. The actors tested creds with WMI against a server (wmic /node:X /user:administrator ... os get caption), RDPed into that server, failed to run a DLL beacon, then ran a PowerShell CS beacon. For the next hour they made RDP connections to other servers. Pivoting from a domain controller, they copied ttsel.exe (Quantum) to each host's C$ share and detonated it via PsExec (custom service 'mstdc') and WMI, encrypting all hosts (README_TO_DECRYPT.html). No overt exfiltration was observed.

detection_moments.description: IcedID ISO/LNK executed via rundll32 on the beachhead; discovery + scheduled-task persistence; ~2h later Cobalt Strike via process hollowing.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the user clicks on the LNK file, the IcedID DLL is executed ... Cobalt Strike was deployed using process hollowing and injection techniques' - Quantum Ransomware, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: LSASS accessed (Task Manager + CS beacon) stealing admin creds; WMI cred test against a server then RDP + PowerShell CS beacon on it.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Suspicious accesses to LSASS process memory ... using both Windows Task Manager and rundll32.exe ... the threat actor tested credentials ... using WMI ... RDP into that server' - Quantum Ransomware

detection_moments.description: ~4h: from a DC pivot, ttsel.exe (Quantum) copied to each host's C$ share and detonated via PsExec (custom service mstdc) and WMI across all hosts.
detection_moments.evidence: 'With their pivot point from one of the domain controllers ... copied the payload, ttsel.exe, to the C$ share of each host ... PsExec and WMI' - Quantum Ransomware
